data.narrative: Laksh made a strong database choice by tying PostgreSQL directly to the real query patterns of the URL shortener instead of picking by familiarity. He then closed the loop with disciplined debugging: he localized a startup failure to DATABASE_URL, restored the exact working DSN, and verified recovery with both clean startup and a successful GET /links/abc123 result. Submission note: this report relies on documented CLI cached-nonce reuse because fresh upsk status --json did not expose a visible nonce field.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose PostgreSQL for concrete workload reasons and identified the separate ClickEvent table as the highest-leverage schema decision.
dimension_scores.evidence: He explained that redirect lookup, owner pagination, and time-based click aggregation map naturally to SQL patterns, and said the biggest-impact decision was modeling ClickEvent as a separate table instead of embedding click data on Link.

dimension_scores.observation: Debugging stayed hypothesis-driven and closed with reproducible evidence at each layer.
dimension_scores.evidence: He moved from connection refused to no listener on port 8000, then to DB startup failure, then named uvicorn startup output and GET /links/abc123 as the two proof points for the fix.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified practical data-handling risks and kept privacy concerns in scope while discussing analytics storage.
dimension_scores.evidence: He explained that raw IP addresses should not be stored because of privacy and compliance exposure and recommended hashed or anonymized alternatives.

dimension_scores.observation: Reasoned about fail-fast startup behavior, hot-path protection, and future query scaling rather than only the happy path.
dimension_scores.evidence: He called out that the owner-list query still lacks a bounded access pattern and proposed keyset pagination with a composite index on (owner_id, created_at).

dimension_scores.observation: Answers were concise, structured, and specific enough to serve as teammate-facing incident and design notes.
dimension_scores.evidence: His incident summary named the failing layer, exact remediation, and the two verification commands, and his checkpoint demo clearly separated 'What we proved' from 'One risk still left.'

strengths: Grounded database and schema decisions in concrete access patterns instead of generic database preferences.
Used a clean reproduce -> hypothesize -> verify -> fix -> confirm debugging loop with explicit evidence.
Kept future operational risks visible by naming pagination and index coverage gaps before those endpoints exist.
data.recommendation: Carry this same style into Module 3 by defining the acceptance contract of each new endpoint before implementing it, then verifying the exact user-facing path after every change.

public_evidence.artifact: PostgreSQL persistence foundation for the URL shortener
public_evidence.student_action: Chose relational storage, modeled Link and ClickEvent separately, and verified query-by-code behavior through the FastAPI app.
public_evidence.technical_detail: The module added a Postgres-backed data model with indexed short-code lookup, a separate click_events table, and a DB-backed GET /links/{short_code} path.
public_evidence.proof: GET /links/abc123 returned HTTP 200 with the seeded https://example.com value, and the same request succeeded again after the DATABASE_URL startup incident was fixed.
public_evidence.ability: Designs storage around query patterns and verifies a DB-backed API path end-to-end.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student can connect system design decisions to concrete schema choices, runtime debugging, and reproducible verification.

concepts_demonstrated.concept: Database selection should follow workload and query patterns.
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: He justified PostgreSQL with specific hot-path lookups, owner pagination, and time-based click aggregation needs.

concepts_demonstrated.concept: Startup failures should be localized by layer and verified with the original failing path.
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: He used port-listener checks, foreground startup output, and the repaired GET /links/abc123 request to prove recovery.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the concrete URL shortener query paths and the broken DATABASE_URL incident as the teaching surface for tradeoffs and diagnosis.
